title: Ising-Machine-Assisted Large Neighborhood Search with Flexibly Tunable Subproblem Size
authors: Koshiro Fujimoto, Masashi Yamashita, Shu Tanaka
abstract: Ising machines are heuristic solvers for combinatorial optimization, but their solution quality can degrade when large-scale constrained problems are solved directly. Ising-machine-assisted large neighborhood search (LNS) instead repeatedly updates a feasible current solution by solving smaller subproblems. An existing feasibility-preserving method for the vehicle routing problem (VRP) re-optimizes the entire routes of selected vehicles and thus cannot adjust the subproblem size finely. We propose LNS-VT, which introduces the number of consecutive steps re-optimized per vehicle as a parameter to control the subproblem size finely while preserving feasibility. For a 300-site, 5-vehicle VRP, its best setting reduced the objective value by approximately 10\% relative to the existing method after 100 iterations, and the appropriate setting changed with the current solution quality. Applying the same principle to the quadratic multiple knapsack problem, we confirmed that an appropriate subproblem size also exists, indicating that subproblem-size control is important in Ising-machine-assisted LNS.
summary: This paper addresses limitations in using Ising machines for large combinatorial problems by proposing $	ext{LNS-VT}$, a method that flexibly controls the size of subproblems solved during Large Neighborhood Search. By tuning the number of variables, the authors achieve significant performance gains over existing methods on VRP and QMKP benchmarks. The work emphasizes that controlling problem structure is as vital as ensuring mathematical feasibility.
main_problem: Improving solution quality for large-scale, constrained combinatorial optimization problems like VRP and QMKP.
main_result: A novel LNS approach ($	ext{LNS-VT}$) that flexibly controls the subproblem size significantly outperforms existing methods by up to 10% on VRP benchmarks.
method: The authors propose an Ising-machine-assisted Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) framework, specifically $	ext{LNS-VT}$, which adaptively tunes the number of variables in the subproblem solved at each step while maintaining feasibility.
model_or_system: The problems are modeled using QUBO energy functions derived from combinatorial optimization objectives (VRP and QMKP). The core mechanism involves iteratively solving smaller, constrained subproblems using an Ising machine solver.
key_observables: Solution objective value improvement (e.g., 10% reduction in VRP), total profit for QMKP, and the number of binary variables used in the subproblem.
important_parameters: The 'number of consecutive steps re-optimized per vehicle' acts as a crucial control parameter determining the subproblem size; optimal settings vary with solution quality.
main_assumptions: Feasibility preservation is necessary but insufficient; controlling the variable count in the subproblem is critical for performance on Ising machines.
figures_summary: Figure 8 shows that for QMKP, the highest total profit is achieved when the number of binary variables in the subproblem is maintained within a specific range (100 to 150).
paper_structure: The paper first defines the VRP and its QUBO formulation. It then introduces LNS-V and proposes the improved, tunable $	ext{LNS-VT}$ framework. Results are presented for both VRP and QMKP, demonstrating the necessity of subproblem size control.
why_interesting: While focused on classical optimization, the reliance on Ising machines (which map to quantum annealing/computation) makes this highly relevant for understanding how heuristic solvers interact with quantum hardware constraints in complex physical modeling.
